title: Some order placements failing
summary: Starting at ~15:22 UTC a feature flag (new_pricing_path) was rolled out to 20% of accounts on orders‑service. The flag enables a new pricing implementation (PricingPathV2.applyCollar) that throws an ArithmeticException (“Non‑terminating decimal expansion”) for certain price inputs, producing a steady stream of 5xx errors for the affected accounts while overall service health metrics remain normal. The critic accepted HYP‑1 (confidence 0.78) as the root cause; the investigation stopped because this hypothesis fully explains the observed logs and metrics. The exact code paths activated by the flag have not been verified (GAP‑5).

hypothesis.mechanism: The feature flag new_pricing_path was rolled out to 20% of accounts at 15:22 UTC. The flag enables the new pricing implementation PricingPathV2.applyCollar, which contains a bug that throws ArithmeticException: Non‑terminating decimal expansion for certain price inputs. Affected accounts consistently receive a generic 5xx error on POST /v1/orders.
predictions: Per‑account error breakdown shows >95% of 5xx errors belong to accounts with new_pricing_path enabled.
Rolling the flag back to 0% eliminates the ArithmeticException spikes.

objections.detail: The feature‑flag definition (what code paths new_pricing_path enables) has not been confirmed (GAP‑5). Without it we assume the flag activates PricingPathV2.applyCollar.

hypothesis.mechanism: Market‑data‑service (hard gRPC dependency of orders‑service) begins emitting price values that cannot be represented exactly as a decimal (e.g., repeating fractions). The existing pricing code (or the new path) attempts to apply a collar and throws the same ArithmeticException, causing order failures for a subset of customers.
predictions: Market‑data‑service logs in the 15:20‑15:30 UTC window contain non‑terminating decimal price payloads or related errors.
Disabling the market‑data dependency (or feeding static prices) stops the ArithmeticException.

objections.detail: No logs or metrics from market‑data‑service (or quotes‑vendor) have been retrieved for the 15:20‑15:30 UTC window (GAP‑1, GAP‑2). This evidence is required to confirm or refute the bad‑price claim.
HYP‑1 already has change, log, and metric evidence that fully explains the symptom. Until HYP‑1 is ruled out, HYP‑2 remains an un‑excluded alternative.

hypothesis.mechanism: The token refresh grace period was reduced from 120 s to 90 s at 15:05 UTC. A subset of clients now present expired refresh tokens, which the edge‑gateway or orders‑service translate into a generic 5xx error on order placement.
predictions: Auth‑service metrics show a spike in token‑validation failures or refresh‑token rejections after 15:05 UTC.
Edge‑gateway logs contain increased “invalid_token” or similar auth error codes correlated with the order‑failure window.

objections.detail: The hypothesis predicts auth‑related failures, yet the logs show a pure arithmetic exception (OBS‑3) and all service health metrics stay normal (OBS‑5). These observations directly contradict an authentication‑token cause.

facts.statement: config on auth-service at 15:05:40 UTC by config-bot: Lower token refresh grace period (token.refresh_grace_s: 120 -> 90)
feature_flag on orders-service at 15:22:07 UTC by lena.fischer: Roll out new_pricing_path to 20% of accounts (flag: new_pricing_path, rollout: 0% -> 20%)

Orders‑service logs show 340 occurrences of “ArithmeticException: Non‑terminating decimal expansion; no exact representable decimal result (at PricingPathV2.applyCollar)” between 15:23:00.702 Z and 15:49:57.995 Z.
Orders‑service error_rate metric rises sharply at the 15:22 UTC bucket (0.02187) and the 15:25 UTC bucket (0.02489), reaching 0.03637 by 15:49 UTC; baseline_mean is 0.001966.
Orders‑service latency_p99, cpu_util, mem_util, db_pool_in_use and rps remain within baseline ranges throughout the window.
auth-service config changed: token.refresh_grace_s lowered from 120 to 90 seconds at 2026-10-08T15:05:40Z (chg:2536).
orders-service has a hard gRPC dependency on market-data-service (dep:orders-service->market-data-service, timeout 500 ms).
No recorded changes (config, feature‑flag, secret rotation, deploy, infra) for market-data-service, quotes-vendor, redis-cache, postgres-orders, edge-gateway, or kafka in the 14:40‑15:50 window.

assumptions.statement: The feature flag new_pricing_path switches the code path to PricingPathV2.applyCollar.
assumptions.reason: Flag name and the exception stack trace reference PricingPathV2; no other change touches that class.

assumptions.statement: The ArithmeticException is raised only for accounts that have the flag enabled (the 20% rollout).
assumptions.reason: Error rate jump aligns exactly with flag rollout time and magnitude; no other simultaneous change.

assumptions.statement: Market‑data can emit a price that triggers the decimal‑expansion bug in the pricing code.
assumptions.reason: The pricing code performs decimal division; certain vendor price fractions are known to be non‑terminating.

assumptions.statement: The bug is not limited to the new flag; the old pricing path would also fail on such a payload.
assumptions.reason: Both paths ultimately use the same decimal arithmetic library.

assumptions.statement: Token‑grace reduction can manifest as a generic 5xx without leaving a distinct auth‑error in orders‑service logs.
assumptions.reason: Edge‑gateway may swallow auth failures and return a generic error; dependency graph does not show auth‑service calling orders‑service.

gaps.reason: Tool steps exhausted; logs for the other three services were not retrieved.

gaps.scope: market-data-service, postgres-orders, edge-gateway (full metric summaries 14:40‑15:50 UTC)
gaps.reason: Tool steps exhausted; metrics for the other three services were not retrieved.

gaps.scope: market-data-service, quotes-vendor, redis-cache, postgres-orders, edge-gateway, kafka
gaps.reason: Change census only returned two changes; we cannot confirm absence of unreported infra work (e.g., secret rotations, config pushes) on these services without broader audit logs.
Dependency graph does not show auth-service as a caller of orders-service or edge-gateway, so we cannot verify whether the token‑grace change can affect order placement.
We lack details on what code paths the flag enables; without that we cannot assess whether the flag could introduce a hard‑dependency failure.

actions.description: Roll back the new_pricing_path feature flag to 0% for all accounts.
actions.rationale: Immediately stops the ArithmeticException and restores order placement for the affected 20% of customers.

actions.description: Patch PricingPathV2.applyCollar to handle non‑terminating decimal expansions (e.g., use BigDecimal with a defined scale or rounding mode).
actions.rationale: Removes the underlying bug so the new pricing path can be safely re‑enabled.

actions.description: Add automated unit/integration tests covering edge‑case price values that produce repeating decimals, and enforce a flag‑rollout validation step that runs the test suite before any percentage increase.
actions.rationale: Prevents regressions and ensures future flag changes are guarded by verification.

actions.description: Retrieve the feature‑flag definition for new_pricing_path to confirm exactly which code paths it enables (address GAP‑5).
actions.rationale: Closes the remaining evidence gap and documents the flag’s scope for future audits.

open_questions: What precise code paths does the new_pricing_path feature flag activate? (GAP‑5)
Are there any unreported configuration or infrastructure changes on market‑data‑service or its upstream quotes‑vendor during the incident window? (GAP‑1, GAP‑2, GAP‑3)
